talks.title: Identity Crisis: Online Account Opening Fraud
talks.teaser: Analyzes synthetic identities, mule networks, and automated bot attacks targeting new online account opening workflows.
talks.summary:
Cyber fraud expert Uri Rivner examines the growing threat of automated and synthetic identity fraud targeting online account opening (NAO) systems across digital banks and fintech platforms [00:00]. Rivner tracks the evolution of financial cybercrime from traditional credit card skimming and account takeover toward synthetic identity creation—where criminal syndicates combine fabricated personal details with legitimate, unmonitored Social Security numbers (such as those belonging to minors) to establish pristine credit profiles [20:00].

The presentation explores the limitations of conventional identity verification methods, including credit bureau checks and document scans, which frequently fail to distinguish synthetic applications from legitimate customers [13:20]. To counter this, Rivner details behavioral biometrics as a transformative defense layer. He demonstrates how tracking user interactions during the onboarding flow—such as keystroke dynamics, copy-paste patterns, typing speed, and navigation pauses—reveals the automated scripts and fraudulent operators behind the keyboard without relying on static PII [26:46].

Rivner analyzes real-world fraud metrics and attack campaigns observed during the shift toward remote banking amid pandemic relief programs [33:38]. He provides financial institutions with actionable architectural recommendations, advocating for continuous behavioral risk scoring, anomaly detection at registration, and multi-layered fraud intelligence to stop synthetic accounts before lines of credit are extended [40:37].

talks.title: Online Banking Security
talks.teaser: Examines application layer security, transaction signing vulnerabilities, and authentication weaknesses in online banking platforms.
talks.summary:
Arkadiy Litvinenko, Lead Penetration Tester at BI.ZONE, explores security risks inherent in modern digital banking platforms, analyzing vulnerabilities across web and mobile banking architectures. He outlines how intense commercial competition forces financial institutions to rapidly deploy digital features, frequently introducing logic flaws, API security weaknesses, and authentication oversights.

Litvinenko details remote banking architecture and API communication models at 03:00, followed by frontend and client-side testing methodologies at 10:00. He walks through real-world attack scenarios, including currency exchange rounding attacks at 20:00 where fractional cent truncation enables illicit profit. At 30:00, he analyzes flawed OTP (One-Time Password) rate limiting that allows brute-force transaction approvals, insecure pseudorandom number generators in financial workflows at 40:00, and mobile client flaws where biometric and PIN authentication fail to properly protect KeyStore/KeyChain tokens at 48:00.

talks.title: Making Sense of EMV Card Data
talks.teaser: Decodes the complex transaction flow, cryptographic authorizations, and data elements embedded in EMV chip cards.
talks.summary:
Professor Steven Murdoch, a leading financial cryptography and smart card security researcher at University College London, delivers a technical masterclass on decoding and analyzing EMV (Europay, Mastercard, Visa) chip card communications [00:03]. Murdoch explains the ISO/IEC 7816 physical and transmission protocols governing contact smart cards, detailing how cards and point-of-sale (POS) terminals exchange Application Protocol Data Units (APDUs) via commands like SELECT AID, GET PROCESSING OPTIONS, and READ RECORD [12:00].

The presentation focuses on parsing the hierarchical Tag-Length-Value (TLV) data structures defined by the EMV specification [19:01]. Murdoch walks through the bitwise decoding of single-byte and multi-byte tags (such as 9Fxx prefixes), card risk management lists (CDOL1/CDOL2 in tag 8C), application interchange profiles, and cryptogram generation [25:39]. He explains the cryptographic mechanics of cardholder verification, exploring the historical evolution from offline PIN verification values (PVV) to dynamic data authentication (DDA) and combined data authentication (CDA) [31:53].

Murdoch reviews notable vulnerabilities discovered in EMV transaction flows, including the famous "No-PIN" attack where manipulated terminal responses tricked POS systems into processing stolen chip cards without requiring a valid PIN [05:41]. He demonstrates open-source decoding tools and provides researchers with methodologies for safely capturing, parsing, and verifying smart card transactions [37:41].
